REQ-M3-007, WP-104 (RSK-026; ADR-0013 decision 9): after a request times out the virtio-blk driver publishes nothing more to the device. Every request shares one header, one status byte, one data buffer and the same three descriptors, and a completion is taken by its position in the used ring, so a request the driver gave up could still complete later and be taken for the next one, and a later write's bytes could reach the earlier request's sector. The case reads one pattern sector (before=ok, pattern=1: the shared buffer now holds that sector), fills its own buffer with a guard byte and arms the test kernel's hook, which withholds the next request from the device (not published, no notify) and shortens its wait so the driver's own timeout branch runs: that read answers K_E_BLK_TIMEOUT, and the block layer writes the line `kernel|blk|stopped|op=read|sector=131064|code=K_E_BLK_TIMEOUT`, once in the whole run (max_counts: the four refusals after it write none). Then four requests are each refused with K_E_BLK_NEEDS_RESET: a read of the timed-out request's sector, a write to that sector of the bytes it already holds, a flush, and a read past the end of the device (refused as stopped, not as out of range). The caller's buffer keeps the guard after the timed-out read and the refused read (caller_kept=1: these two failed reads hand back nothing); after the refused write the shared buffer still holds the first sector (buffer_kept=1: the refusal comes before the copy); the driver's available index did not move across the four refusals (published=0); no frame is left; exit 33. Not shown by this case: a late completion from a real device (the withheld request never reaches the device); the order of the refusal against the missing-FLUSH shortcut (the lab device offers FLUSH); that the stop lasts beyond these four requests (the flag is never cleared: read in the code, not measured).

The test kernel's hook ends the volume, for the allocator, just before a chosen free cluster (two free clusters ahead when the case arms it): the allocator's own scan runs to that end and answers full, and a cluster freed below it is found again. Before the volume is ended, file D is given one cluster and then an append whose ninth and last write, the entry, the block layer's hook refuses (d_fault=K_E_FS_IO): its chain holds two clusters and its size one (d_long=1; files.md v1.6). File A, empty: three clusters with two left are refused (a_big=K_E_FS_DISK_FULL) and the file stays empty with no first cluster, in its stored entry, its node and its chain (a_big_size=0, a_big_node=0, a_big_chain=0); two clusters fit and are written (a_fit=1024); one byte more, at the end of the last cluster, is refused (a_more=K_E_FS_DISK_FULL); a write from the second cluster that overwrites it and needs a third is refused (a_span=K_E_FS_DISK_FULL), and after both the file holds its 1024 bytes in its entry, its node, its chain and its bytes, and the same open reads them from 0 (a_size=1024, a_node=1024, a_chain=2, a_whole=1, a_read=1024); an overwrite of both clusters, which needs no new cluster, succeeds with nothing left (a_over=1024, a_over_whole=1). File B, half a cluster (256 bytes): a write from the middle of its cluster that needs a second one is refused and the file is what it was (b_span=K_E_FS_DISK_FULL, b_size=256, b_whole=1); a write to the end of its own cluster succeeds (b_fill=256, b_chain=1, b_filled=1). File C, empty: one byte is refused and it stays empty with no first cluster (c_none=K_E_FS_DISK_FULL, c_node=0, c_chain=0, c_empty=1). File D, with nothing left: its second cluster's bytes are written into the cluster its chain already holds, the call needing none (d_into=512, d_chain=2, d_whole=1): the clusters a file has are counted along its chain, not from its size. M3.oracle: REQ-M3-007, WP-117 (RSK-027; ADR-0013 decision 9; files.md v1.9): once the disk has stopped, every file call answers an I/O error and none answers from memory, a process sees ERR_IO, and the file system says so once. First boot: file A (three clusters) is written and closed; file B (two clusters) is open twice by the kernel, one position at its end and one at 0; file T was written two clusters through one open and emptied through another, so that open's position is past the size. The test kernel's hook is armed to withhold from the device the second disk write from then on, and the application stopio is run. It opens B, reads its 1024 bytes to the end and deletes A: the delete's first write is the entry and its second, the first to a FAT copy, is the withheld one, so the driver's own timeout branch answers that request and stops the disk inside the process's call (one line kernel|blk|stopped). The application exits 0x5709 only if the delete answered ERR_IO and so did each of the thirteen calls it then made through the system-call layer: a read at the end of its open, a seek, a write of no bytes, a stat, a create, a sync, a directory listing and an open of an existing file; then five calls a working disk would refuse for their arguments: an open whose path has no leading slash, an open with flags that are none, a stat whose path has no leading slash and a read through a handle that was closed, the four for which the system-call layer's question, asked before a path, flags or a handle are looked at, is what answers ERR_IO; and a seek past the size, which the file layer already refuses with ERR_IO before it compares the position (app_exit=0x5709; any other exit code is the number of the step that answered something else). In both rounds the wait leaves the interrupt flag as it found it, and it found it off (the kernel requires irq_before = irq_after; the case requires `|irq_before=0|irq_after=0`: the test kernel's boot thread runs with interrupts off outside its waits). The kernel judges each round and prints `|ktest|wait_deadline|spinner_prio=

|ok=1|` with late, limit, polls, spins, resumed and the two flags; no frame is left; exit 33. A spinner gives up by itself after 400 ticks, so a kernel that starves the waiter fails with late about 350 instead of hanging.
